title: Cross-border model compliance & supply migration plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Some enterprise prospects require that models and inference endpoints run in specific legal jurisdictions (EU/UK/APAC) or meet local data residency and compliance constraints. We lack a concise playbook that maps competing model vendors, open-model availability per region, license restrictions, and migration effort to enable sales and platform teams to commit to fallbacks and onboarding timelines.

Goal: Deliver a research-backed operational plan and a prioritized vendor/model migration matrix that answers: (1) Which model variants are available per region and under what licensing constraints? (2) What is the estimated engineering effort to provision per-region endpoints (hosted, dedicated, private)? (3) What contractual or procurement steps are required for enterprise customers? (4) A decision tree for recommending fallback variants when the primary model is unavailable due to regional restrictions.

Deliverables: 1) Model availability matrix (region x model) with license notes and latency bucket; 2) Migration effort estimates (S/M/L) per model for Hosted, Dedicated, Private; 3) Risk register for IP/license/regulatory blockers; 4) Pre-approved partner shortlist for APAC and EU procurement; 5) Confluence playbook + a one-page cheat sheet for sales/security reviews.

Acceptance criteria: The playbook must be reviewed by Legal (compliance signoff), validated by Infra (deployment feasibility), and contain bootstrap runbooks for two example enterprise customers (finance EU customer, healthcare APAC customer). The matrix must include measured latency samples from prod-like regions or simulator runs.

Why now: Increasing inbound from regulated customers and three active deals where model residency is a gating factor. Competitive sales motion also shows customers asking about fallbacks and SLA guarantees tied to geography.
